notes: TBox subject insert. The plural forms the prompts offer are surfaces of the ending they use (one individual per ending). Q2 and Q3 are fol (closed lists) and, since 2026-10-31, determinate 'no' (FINDINGS A1), so the record has no worlds.
edit: SkarnovishNoun ⊑ EnglishNoun and plural_formed_with value en_ending

queries.not_checked: fol (closed world): 'the only English plurals' over a closed list
fol (closed world): 'the only English plural' over a closed list

fol.notes: Nouns are strings; plural_form is the ATTRIBUTES.md attribute. The edit is the class rule plus the existence of the group ('a small group of nouns'); 'newly coined' keeps them apart from ox, child and brother. The stored closed lists are presuppositions the insert gives up (FINDINGS A1).

en_plurals.says: 'Oxen', 'children' and 'brethren' are the plurals of 'ox', 'child' and 'brother'; they are English nouns, not archaic, dialect or jocular forms.

three_only.says: Leaving aside archaic, dialect and jocular forms, the English plurals in '-en' are 'oxen', 'children' and 'brethren'. (stored closed list)
three_only.z3: ForAll(n, Implies(And(english_noun(n), Not(archaic_or_jocular(n)), endswith(plural_form(n), "en")), Or(n == "ox", n == "child", n == "brother")))

oxen_only.says: 'Oxen' is the only plain '-en' plural: 'children' adds '-ren' and 'brethren' changes the vowel. (stored closed list)
oxen_only.z3: ForAll(n, Implies(And(english_noun(n), Not(archaic_or_jocular(n)), plural_form(n) == n + "en"), n == "ox"))

edit: ForAll(n, Implies(skarnovish(n), And(english_noun(n), newly_coined(n), Not(archaic_or_jocular(n)), plural_form(n) == n + "en")))

queries.ask: ForAll(n, Implies(And(english_noun(n), Not(archaic_or_jocular(n)), endswith(plural_form(n), "en")), Or(n == "ox", n == "child", n == "brother")))
ForAll(n, Implies(And(english_noun(n), Not(archaic_or_jocular(n)), plural_form(n) == n + "en"), n == "ox"))

label_corrections.why: A closed list is a nominal (EnPluralNoun and not Archaic ⊑ {ox, child, brother}); the edit's class with an existing member contradicts it. Expressible in DL with nominals, no arithmetic.
As q2, a singleton nominal {ox} over the class of plain '-en' plurals.
